response.sql: WITH per_scope AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS scope, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS n_fees FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT scope, avg_net_fee_rate, n_fees, avg_net_fee_rate - (SELECT AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) FROM per_scope) AS diff_from_mean_of_scope_avgs FROM per_scope ORDER BY scope

assumptions.assumption: Inner joins drop unmatched fees, orders and users. Each recordvault and userstamp is assumed unique, so the joins don't duplicate fee rows.
The net rate is feerate - rebrate. Fee rows where either value is NULL give a NULL net rate, so they are left out of both the average and the count.

The 'simple mean of the scope averages' is the unweighted mean of the per-scope averages, not the overall fee-level average. The deviation is the scope average minus that mean. No rounding is applied.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat a NULL rebate rate as 0, so every fee row with a fee rate counts toward the average and the count.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_scope AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS scope, AVG(f.feerate - COALESCE(f.rebrate,0)) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(f.feerate) AS n_fees FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT scope, avg_net_fee_rate, n_fees, avg_net_fee_rate - (SELECT AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) FROM per_scope) AS diff_from_mean_of_scope_avgs FROM per_scope ORDER BY scope
